typedef struct Node{
	int key;
	struct Node*left;
	struct Node*right;
	int height;
}Node;
int height(Node*N){
	if(N==NULL)return 0;
	return N->height;
}
int max(int a, int b){
	return(a>b)?a:b;
}
Node*newNode(int key){
	Node*node=(Node*)malloc(sizeof(Node));
	node->key=key;
	node->left=node->right=NULL;
	node->height=1;
	return node;
}
Node*rightRotate(Node*y){
	Node*x = y->left;
	Node*T2=x->right;
	x->right=y;
	y->left=T2;
	y->height=max(height(y->left),height(y->right))+1;
	x->height=max(height(x->left),height(x->right))+1;
	return x;
}
Node*leftRotate(Node*x){
	Node*y=x->right;
	Node*T2=y->left;
	y->left=x;
	x->right=T2;
	x->height=max(height(x->left),height(x->right))+1;
	y->height=max(height(y->left),height(y->left))+1;
	return y;
}
int getBalance(Node*N){

	if(node==NULL)

	if(key<node->key)

	node->height=1+max(height(node->left),height(node->right));
	int balance=getBalance(node);
	if(balance >1 && key <node->left->key)return rightRotate(node);
	if(balance < -1 && key <node->right-> key)return leftRotate(node);
	if(balance > 1 && key > node->left->key){
		node->left=leftRotate(node->left);
		return rightRotate(node);
	}
	if (balance <-1 && key < node->right->key){
		node->right=rightRotate(node->right);
		return leftRotate(node);
	}
	return node;
}
Node*minValueNode(Node*node){
	Node*current=node;
	while(current->left)
		current=current->left;
	return current;
}

S.No: 2 Exp. Name: Operation of B-Tree - Insertion, Deletion and Search Date: 2026-10-06
Aim:

Write a C program to construct a B-Tree of a given minimum degree. First, insert a list of keys into the B-Tree and print the inorder traversal after all insertions. Then, delete a given set of keys from the B-Tree and again print the inorder traversal. Finally, search for a specific key in the current B-Tree and print whether it is found or not.


Input Format:

  • The first line contains a single integer t, the minimum degree of the B-Tree.
  • The second line contains an integer n, representing the number of keys to be inserted.
  • The third line contains n space-separated integers — the keys to be inserted into the B-Tree.
  • The fourth line contains an integer d, the number of keys to delete.
  • The fifth line contains d space-separated integers — the keys to be deleted from the B-Tree.
  • The sixth line contains a single integer k — the key to be searched in the B-Tree.


Output Format:

  • The first line of output should display the inorder traversal of the B-Tree after all insertions, with each key separated by a space.
  • The second line should display the inorder traversal of the B-Tree after all deletions, with each key separated by a space.
  • The third line should print Found if the search key exists in the B-Tree. If the key is not present, print Not Found instead.



Note: Refer to the test cases for better understanding.

#include<stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
typedef struct BTreeNode {
int *keys;
int t;
struct BTreeNode **C;
int n;
bool leaf;
} BTreeNode;
// Create a new node
BTreeNode* createNode(int t, bool leaf) {
BTreeNode* node = (BTreeNode*)malloc(sizeof(BTreeNode));
node->t = t;
node->leaf = leaf;
node->keys = (int*)malloc((2 * t - 1) * sizeof(int));
node->C = (BTreeNode**)malloc((2 * t) * sizeof(BTreeNode*));
node->n = 0;
return node;
}
// Inorder traversal (no trailing dot)
void inorder(BTreeNode* root) {
if (!root) return;
for (int i = 0; i < root->n; i++) {
if (!root->leaf)
inorder(root->C[i]);
printf("%d ", root->keys[i]);
}
if (!root->leaf)
inorder(root->C[root->n]);
}
// Search a key
bool search(BTreeNode* root, int k) {
int i = 0;
while (i < root->n && k > root->keys[i])
i++;
if (i < root->n && root->keys[i] == k)
return true;
if (root->leaf)
return false;
return search(root->C[i], k);
}

It should then read the number of deletions to perform, delete the root (minimum element) that many times, and display the heap both before and after the deletions.


Input Format:

  • The first line contains an integer n, representing the number of elements to insert into the heap.
  • The second line contains n space-separated integers — the values to insert into the heap.
  • The third line contains an integer k, representing the number of times the root (minimum element) should be deleted from the heap.


Output Format:

#include <stdio.h>
#define MAX_SIZE 1000

int heap[MAX_SIZE];
int size = 0;

void swap(int* a, int* b) {
	int t = *a;
	*a = *b;
	*b = t;
}
void heapifyUp (int i) {
	while (i > 0 && heap[(i - 1) /2] > heap[i]) {
		swap(&heap[i], &heap[(i - 1) / 2]);
		i = (i - 1) / 2;
	}
}
void insert(int value) {
	heap[size] = value;
	heapifyUp(size);
	size++;
}

void heapifyDown(int i) {
	int smallest = i;
	int l = 2 * i+1;
	int r = 2 * i+2;
	if(l < size && heap[l]< heap[smallest]) 
		smallest =l;
	if(r < size && heap[r] < heap[smallest]) 
		smallest =r;
	if (smallest !=i){
		swap(&heap[i], &heap[smallest]);
		heapifyDown(smallest);
	}
}
void deleteMin() {
	if (size == 0) return;
	heap[0] = heap[size-1];
	size--;
	heapifyDown(0);
}

#include<stdio.h>
#define MAX_SIZE 1000
int heap[MAX_SIZE];
int size = 0;
void swap(int*a, int*b){
	int t= *a;
	*a =*b;
	*b =t;
}
void heapifyUp(int index){
	while (index >0 && heap[(index-1) /2] < heap[index]){
		swap(&heap[index],&heap[(index-1) /2]);
		index = (index-1) /2;
	}
}
void insert(int value){
	heap[size]= value;
	heapifyUp(size);
	size++;
	heapifyUp(size - 1);
}
void heapifyDown(int index){
	int largest =index;
	int left =2* index +1;
	int right=2*index +2;

	if (left < size && heap[left]> heap[largest])
		largest =left;
	if(right < size && heap[right]>heap[largest])
		largest = right;
	if (largest !=index){
		swap(&heap[index], &heap[largest]);
		heapifyDown(largest);
	}
}
void deleteMax(){
	if (size == 0)
		return;
	heap[0] = heap[size-1];
	size--;
	heapifyDown(0);
}

void BFS(int start) {

struct Node {
    int vertex;
    struct Node *next;
};

struct Node *adj[100];
int visited[100];

void addEdge(int u, int v) {
    struct Node *newNode = (struct Node *)malloc(sizeof(struct Node));
    newNode->vertex = v;
    newNode->next = NULL;

    if (adj[u] == NULL || adj[u]->vertex > v) {
        newNode->next = adj[u];
        adj[u] = newNode;
    } else {
        struct Node *temp = adj[u];

        while (temp->next != NULL && temp->next->vertex < v)
            temp = temp->next;

        newNode->next = temp->next;
        temp->next = newNode;
    }
}

void DFS(int start) {
    struct Node *temp;

    visited[start] = 1;
    printf("%d ", start);

    temp = adj[start];

    while (temp != NULL) {
        if (!visited[temp->vertex])
            DFS(temp->vertex);
        temp = temp->next;
    }
}

#include <stdio.h>

void quickSort(int a[], int low, int high) {
    int i, j, pivot, temp;

    if (low < high) {
        pivot = a[low];
        i = low;
        j = high;

        while (i < j) {
            while (a[i] <= pivot && i < high)
                i++;

            while (a[j] > pivot)
                j--;

            if (i < j) {
                temp = a[i];
                a[i] = a[j];
                a[j] = temp;
            }
        }

        temp = a[low];
        a[low] = a[j];
        a[j] = temp;

        quickSort(a, low, j - 1);
        quickSort(a, j + 1, high);
    }
}

        scanf("%d", &a[i]);

#include <stdio.h>

void merge(int a[], int low, int mid, int high) {
    int i = low, j = mid + 1, k = 0;
    int temp[100];

    while (i <= mid && j <= high) {
        if (a[i] <= a[j])
            temp[k++] = a[i++];
        else
            temp[k++] = a[j++];
    }

    while (i <= mid)
        temp[k++] = a[i++];

    while (j <= high)
        temp[k++] = a[j++];

    for (i = low, k = 0; i <= high; i++, k++)
        a[i] = temp[k];
}

void mergeSort(int a[], int low, int high) {
    int mid;

    if (low < high) {
        mid = (low + high) / 2;

        mergeSort(a, low, mid);
        mergeSort(a, mid + 1, high);

        merge(a, low, mid, high);
    }
}

int main() {
    int n, a[100], i;

        scanf("%d", &a[i]);

We earn the profit associated with the job if and only if the job is completed by its deadline. Find the number of jobs done and themaximum profit.


Note:Jobs will be given in the form (Job Id, Deadline, Profit) associated with that Job. The deadline of the job is the time by which the job needs to be completed to earn the profit.


Input Format:

  • The first line contains an integer N representing the number of jobs.
  • The next N lines each contain three space-separated integers: {Job ID, Job Deadline, Job Profit} — representing one job per line.


Output Format

  • Two integers separated by a space:
  • The first integer represents the number of jobs done.The second integer represents the maximum profit obtained.


Constraints:

  • 1≤N≤105
  • 1≤Deadline≤N
  • 1≤Profit≤500

Input:

2 1 10 
3 1 40 
4 1 30

Aim:

You are given n items, each with a specific weight and value. You have a knapsack with a maximum capacity W. Your goal is to select a subset of these items such that the total weight is less than or equal to W, and the total value is as large as possible.


This is the classic 0/1 Knapsack problem, where each item can either be included once or excluded from the knapsack.


Input Format:

  • The first line contains an integer n, representing the number of items to consider for the knapsack.
  • The second line contains n space-separated integers, representing the weights of the items.
  • The third line contains n space-separated integers, representing the values of the items, corresponding to their weights.
  • The fourth line contains an integer W, representing the capacity of the knapsack.


Output Format:

  • Print the maximum profit that can be obtained by selecting items such that their combined weight does not exceed the knapsack capacity.


Note: Refer to the test cases for better understanding.

dynamicKs.c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
	int n, capacity;
	scanf("%d", &n);
	int weight[n], value[n];
	for (int i=0; i<n; i++) 
		scanf("%d", &weight[i]);
	for (int i=0; i<n; i++)
		scanf("%d", &value[i]);
	scanf("%d", &capacity);
	int dp[capacity +1];
	for (int w=0; w <= capacity; w++)
		dp[w] = 0;
	for (int i=0; i<n; i++) {
		for (int w = capacity; w>= weight[i]; w--){
			int include =dp[w- weight[i]] + value[i];
			if (include> dp[w])
				dp[w] = include;
		}
	}
	printf("%d\n", dp[capacity]);

	return 0;
}

Aim:

Write a C program to solve the N-Queens problem using backtracking. The goal is to place N queens on an N×N chessboard such that no two queens attack each other. A queen can attack another queen if they share the same row, column, or diagonal. Your program should print the first valid configuration of the board found by placing queens from left to right and top to bottom, using a backtracking approach. The board must be displayed as an N×N matrix where a cell contains 1 if a queen is placed there, and 0 otherwise. If no solution exists for the given value of N, print a message indicating that no solution exists.


Input Format:

  • A single integer N — the number of queens and the size of the chessboard.


Output Format:

  • If a solution exists, print an N×N matrix consisting of 0s and 1s, where 1 represents a queen.
  • If no solution exists, print: "No solution exists for N = <value>".
  • Each row of the matrix should be printed on a new line, with space-separated values.

#include<stdio.h>
#include<conio.h>
#include<stdbool.h>
#define MAX 20
int board [MAX][MAX];
void printSolution(int n) {
	int i;
	for( i=0; i<n; i++) {
	int j;
		for(j=0; j<n; j++) {
			printf("%d ", board[i][j]);
		}
		printf("\n");
	}
}
bool isSafe(int row, int col, int n) {
	int i,j;
	for(i=0; i<row; i++) {
		if(board[i][col]==1) return false;
	}
	for(i=row, j=col; i>=0 &&j>=0; i--, j--) {
		if(board[i][j] == 1) return false;
	}
	for(i=row, j=col;i>=0 && j<n; i--, j++) {
		if(board[i][j]==1) return false;
	}
	return true;
} 
bool solveNQueens(int row, int n) {
	if(row == n) {
		return true;
	}
	int col;
	for(col=0; col<n; col++) {
		if(isSafe(row, col, n)) {
			board[row][col] =1;
			if(solveNQueens(row+1, n)) {
				return true;
			}
			board[row][col]=0;
		}
	}
	return false;

		return 0;

	int i,j;
	for(i=0; i<n; i++) {
		for(j=0; j<n; j++) { 
			board[i][j] =0;
		}
	}
	if(solveNQueens(0, n)) {
		printSolution(n);

}

#include<stdio.h>
int n;
int w;
int maxprofit =0;
int values[100], weights[100];
void knapsack(int i, int currentWeight, int currentValue) {
	if (i==n) {
		if (currentValue > maxprofit) 
			maxprofit = currentValue;
		return;
	}
	if (currentWeight + weights[i] <= w) {
		knapsack(i+1, currentWeight + weights[i], currentValue + values[i]);
	}
	knapsack (i+1, currentWeight, currentValue);
}
int main() {
	scanf("%d", &n);
	for (int i=0; i<n; i++) {
		scanf("%d%d", &values[i], &weights[i]);
		
	}
	scanf("%d", &w);
	knapsack(0,0,0);
	printf("%d\n", maxprofit);
	return 0;
}

#include<stdio.h>
#define INF 999999
int main() 
{
	int n;
	scanf("%d", &n);
	int cost[10][10];
	for(int i=0; i<n; i++) {
		for(int j=0;j<n; j++) {
			scanf("%d", &cost[i][j]);
			if(cost[i][j]==-1) {
				cost[i][j]=INF;
			}
		}
	}
	int minCost=INF;
	if(n==3){
		int tour1=cost[0][1]+cost[1][2]+cost[2][0];
		int tour2=cost[0][2]+cost[2][1]+cost[1][0];
		if(tour1<minCost)minCost=tour1;
		if(tour2<minCost)minCost=tour2;
	}
	if(n==4){
		int tour1=cost[0][1]+cost[1][2]+cost[2][3]+cost[3][0];
		int tour2=cost[0][1]+cost[1][3]+cost[3][2]+cost[2][0];
		int tour3=cost[0][2]+cost[2][1]+cost[1][3]+cost[3][0];
		int tour4=cost[0][2]+cost[2][3]+cost[3][1]+cost[1][0];
		int tour5=cost[0][3]+cost[3][1]+cost[2][1]+cost[1][0];
		int tour6=cost[0][3]+cost[3][2]+cost[2][1]+cost[1][0];
		if(tour1<minCost)minCost=tour1;
		if(tour2<minCost)minCost=tour2;
		if(tour3<minCost)minCost=tour3;
		if(tour4<minCost)minCost=tour4;
		if(tour5<minCost)minCost=tour5;
		if(tour6<minCost)minCost=tour6;
	}
	if(minCost==INF){
		printf("No possible tour\n");
	}
	else {
		printf("%d\n", minCost);
	}
	return 0;
}
